sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: SRE and production-operations interview questions cover the role that owns reliability for every modern Java backend — incident response and runbooks, postmortems and the blameless culture, on-call rotation design, error budgets and SLO-driven engineering, capacity planning, chaos engineering, the production-debug toolkit (jstack, jmap, async-profiler, JFR, eBPF), and the questions interviewers ask to test calm under pressure ("P0 fires — walk me through the first 15 minutes"). Pair this with the Observability page for the full production-engineering surface.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Production engineering revolves around **incident → postmortem → SLO**.

- **Incident** — declare early; severity guides response, not ego.
- **On-call** — runbooks per alert, paired rotation, fair distribution.
- **Postmortem** — blameless, timeline + 5-whys, action items with owners.
- **Toolkit** — `jstack`, `jmap`, `async-profiler`, JFR, eBPF.
- **Capacity planning** — model peak + headroom + chaos drills.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **MTTR > MTBF** for modern systems — fast recovery beats rare failure.
- **Error budget** — depleted = freeze risky deploys; pure SRE doctrine.
- **Memory leaks in JVM** — heap dump + diff retained sets; `LinkedHashMap` cache without bounds is the classic.
- **Thread dumps** — look for `BLOCKED` clusters, that's the contention.
- **Chaos engineering** — start small, gameday quarterly.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For a P1 I'd declare, mitigate first (rollback / feature flag), preserve evidence, run a blameless postmortem within 48 h with concrete action items, track them to closure, and feed the lesson back into runbooks + alerts."*
